IN THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH  AT INDORE  CRA No. 168 of 2018  (NARAYAN SINGH JATAV AND OTHERS Vs THE STATE OF MADH  Dated : 04-02-2026  Shri Manish Kumar Vijaywargiya, Advocate for the appell  Shri Bhaskar Agrawal, Public Prosecutor for the respond Heard on I.A No.420/2026 , which is third application under Section 430(1) of BNSS (earlier Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C.) for grant of suspension of jail sentence filed on behalf of appellant No.2 - Ghanshyam Singh Jatav S/o Narayan Singh Jatav.
The appellant has been convicted under Sections 302 (2 counts) and 307 of IPC alongwith Section 27 of the Arms Act and sentenced to undergo life imprisonment with fine of Rs.50,000/-, RI for 07 years with fine of Rs.10,000/- and RI for 05 years with fine of Rs.5,000/- respectively with usual default stipulations.

sentences.text: The present application has been filed mainly on the ground that the appellant has already undergone actual jail sentence of more than 10 years.

Counsel for the State has opposed the prayer and submits that present case is one of the case, which falls within the category carved out by the Apex Court in the order dated 05.10.2021 passed in SLP (Criminal) No.4633 of 2021 (Saudan Singh Vs. The State of U.P. and others).

sentences.text: He argued that in the present case, two persons died because of the gun fired and two persons received gun injuries.

After hearing counsel for the parties and considering the submissions 2 CRA-168-2018 of the injured witness Kesar Singh (PW-3) and other witnesses PW-1, PW-2, PW-4 and PW-5, we find that it is a case where allegation is against the present appellant that he had fired on deceased Balram,
who succumbed to death.
Prima-facie, we are of the view that the appellant is not entitled for grant of suspension of jail sentence on the ground of 10 years custodial period.
However, considering the fact that appeal is pending since 2018, we consider it appropriate to direct the appeal to be listed for final hearing.

The appellant has been convicted under Sections 302 (2 counts) and 307 of IPC alongwith Section 27 of the Arms Act and sentenced to undergo life imprisonment with fine of Rs.50,000/-, RI for 07 years with fine of Rs.10,000/- and RI for 05 years with fine of Rs.5,000/- respectively with usual default stipulations.

opennyai_summary.arguments: Counsel for the State has opposed the prayer and submits that present case is one of the case, which falls within the category carved out by the Apex Court in the order dated 05.10.2021 passed in SLP (Criminal) No.4633 of 2021 (Saudan Singh Vs. The State of U.P. and others).
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
He argued that in the present case, two persons died because of the gun fired and two persons received gun injuries.
After hearing counsel for the parties and considering the submissions 2 CRA-168-2018 of the injured witness Kesar Singh (PW-3) and other witnesses PW-1, PW-2, PW-4 and PW-5, we find that it is a case where allegation is against the present appellant that he had fired on deceased Balram,
who succumbed to death.
Prima-facie, we are of the view that the appellant is not entitled for grant of suspension of jail sentence on the ground of 10 years custodial period.
opennyai_summary.decision:
However, considering the fact that appeal is pending since 2018, we consider it appropriate to direct the appeal to be listed for final hearing.
Office is directed to list the appeal for final hearing in the final hearing list in the month of March,
2026.
With the aforesaid, IA No.420/2026 stands rejected.
